evidence.claim: Jokowi ordered his cabinet to stop discussing election delay or extension of the presidential term and said the election delay/extension idea should stop.
evidence.title: Indonesia president seeks to end talk he is angling for a new term
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi ordered his cabinet to stop discussing election delay or extension of the presidential term and said the election delay/extension idea should stop.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with explicit ruler quotation and constitutional context.
evidence.period_fit: Direct April 2022 conduct in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Jokowi statement and cabinet instruction.
contrary_evidence: Reuters notes critics still saw the response as ambiguous rather than an unqualified rejection.
The article also shows the extension idea had already gained momentum among political figures, so this is partly reactive.

evidence.claim: Indonesia remained partly free, the electoral framework was largely democratic but had problematic provisions, and the country continued to have significant pluralism with multiple peaceful transfers of power while facing military influence, online propaganda, and limits on political equality.
evidence.title: Indonesia: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Indonesia remained partly free, the electoral framework was largely democratic but had problematic provisions, and the country continued to have significant pluralism with multiple peaceful transfers of power while facing military influence, online propaganda, and limits on political equality.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major annual democracy assessment with detailed country coding and narrative explanation.
evidence.period_fit: Standing 2022 country baseline, not a single event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited/system-level context; some cabinet military appointments are attributed to Jokowi in the report, but most findings are structural.
contrary_evidence: Much of the content reflects inherited institutions and system-level constraints rather than 2022 presidential choice.
The report is a synthesis, not a direct account of Jokowi's intent.

evidence.claim: The government restricted speech through defamation, hate-speech, blasphemy, and false-information penalties; there were numerous reports of law being used to limit criticism of the government; and the updated criminal code criminalized insulting state institutions and criticizing the president and vice president.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Indonesia
evidence.excerpt: The government restricted speech through defamation, hate-speech, blasphemy, and false-information penalties; there were numerous reports of law being used to limit criticism of the government; and the updated criminal code criminalized insulting state institutions and criticizing the president and vice president.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government human-rights report summarizing 2022 conditions with legal specificity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level, under Jokowi's administration; the report does not isolate Jokowi as the direct author of each restriction.
contrary_evidence: The report also says the constitution provides freedom of expression and that the code was not yet in force by year-end.
This is a broad rights report rather than a direct act by Jokowi.

evidence.claim: HRW said the 2022 criminal code seriously violated human rights and undermined freedom of speech and association; it also noted that Jokowi had previously delayed an earlier draft after mass protests and later ordered cabinet 'socialization' of the bill.
evidence.title: Indonesia: New Criminal Code Disastrous for Rights
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the 2022 criminal code seriously violated human rights and undermined freedom of speech and association; it also noted that Jokowi had previously delayed an earlier draft after mass protests and later ordered cabinet 'socialization' of the bill.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights organization with explicit 2022 legal analysis and historical comparison.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 legislative outcome and a prior ruler response used as comparison.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The passage of the law is a parliamentary act under Jokowi's administration; the earlier delay is directly attributed to Jokowi.
contrary_evidence: The report shows Jokowi had previously responded to protest pressure by delaying an earlier draft, which is a mitigating fact.
The final law was passed by parliament, so the immediate act is not uniquely a presidential decision.

evidence.claim: The new criminal code criminalized insulting the president and vice president, insulting state institutions, blasphemy expansions, and sex outside marriage, with complaints required for some offenses and a three-year implementation window before it takes effect.
evidence.title: Indonesia: New Criminal Code Passed by Parliament
evidence.excerpt: The new criminal code criminalized insulting the president and vice president, insulting state institutions, blasphemy expansions, and sex outside marriage, with complaints required for some offenses and a three-year implementation window before it takes effect.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government legal bulletin with precise statutory summary and enactment date.
evidence.period_fit: Direct late-2022 legal change in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Parliamentary enactment under Jokowi's presidency; not a personal order by Jokowi in the text itself.
contrary_evidence: The article says opponents can seek judicial review and that the law was not yet in force at year-end.
The piece summarizes legal text rather than enforcement outcomes.
